prophet: The idol worshippers once said to the Prophet ﷺ: 'Muhammad, tell us about the family of your Lord.' Then Allah sent down this surah. (Ahmad and At-Tirmidhi, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b.)

The Prophet ﷺ said this surah is worth a third of the Quran. A man had heard another man read 'Say: He is Allah, One' again and again, and he thought it was a small thing. The Prophet ﷺ said: 'By the One who holds my soul in His hand, it is equal to a third of the Quran.' (Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Sa'id.)
He also asked his friends, 'Can one of you read a third of the Quran in one night?' It was hard for them. So he said: 'Allah is One, As-Samad is a third of the Quran.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.)

Aisha told about a man the Prophet ﷺ sent with an army. He always ended his prayer by reading this surah. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'Ask him why he does that.' The man said, 'Because it tells about Ar-Rahman, and I love to read it.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Tell him that Allah loves him.' (Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim.)

A man from the Ansar led the prayer in the mosque of Quba. He read this surah in every rakah, and then another surah. His friends told him to stop, but he said he loved it. The Prophet ﷺ told him: 'Your love for it will take you to Paradise.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.)

Abu Hurayrah was walking with the Prophet ﷺ when they heard a man read this surah. The Prophet ﷺ said, 'It is sure.' Abu Hurayrah asked, 'What is sure?' He said, 'Paradise.' (Told by Malik. At-Tirmidhi said it is hasan sahih gharib.)
scholars: Ikrimah said that different people believed different things. The Jews said, 'We worship Uzayr, the son of Allah.' The Christians said, 'We worship the Messiah, the son of Allah.' The fire worshippers said, 'We worship the sun and the moon.' The idol worshippers said, 'We worship idols.' So Allah told His Messenger ﷺ to say: 'He is Allah, One.' (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Ibn Kathir explains that 'Ahad' (One) means the only One. He has no equal, no helper, and nothing is like Him. This word can only be used for Allah, because He is perfect in everything about Him.

The book Tanwir al-Miqbas (from Ibn Abbas) says the people of Quraysh asked the Prophet ﷺ to describe his Lord, and asked if He was made of gold or silver. So Allah sent down this surah to tell about Himself.

prophet: A man in the mosque asked Allah with the words of this surah: 'You are the One, the One everyone needs. You do not give birth and You were not born, and no one is like You.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'By the One who holds my soul, he has asked Allah by His Greatest Name. When someone asks Allah with it, He gives, and when someone calls on Him with it, He answers.' (An-Nasa'i. At-Tirmidhi said it is hasan gharib.)
scholars: Ibn Abbas said As-Samad means the One that all of creation needs for everything they need and ask for. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)

Ibn Abbas also said: He is the Master who is perfect in His power, the most noble, the most great, the most patient, the One who knows everything, and the most wise. No one else is like this. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)
Abu Wa'il said As-Samad is the Master whose control is complete. (Told by Ibn Kathir.)

A report in At-Tirmidhi's book says As-Samad is the One who does not give birth and was not born. This is because everything that is born will die, and everything that dies leaves things behind. Allah does not die and leaves nothing behind.
The book Al-Jalalayn says As-Samad is the One we always go to when we need something.

prophet: The Prophet ﷺ said: 'No one is more patient with a hurtful thing he hears than Allah. People say He has a son, but He is the One who gives them food and cures them.' (Sahih al-Bukhari.)

In a hadith qudsi (words of Allah that the Prophet ﷺ told us), Allah said: 'The son of Adam says no to Me, and he has no right to. He says bad things about Me, and he has no right to. When he says that I will not make him again as I made him the first time, making him again is easier than the first time. When he says that I have taken a son, that is a bad thing to say. I am One, the One everyone needs. I do not give birth, and I was not born, and no one is like Me.' (Sahih al-Bukhari, from Abu Hurayrah.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir explains: Allah has no child, no parent and no wife. Mujahid said that 'no one is like Him' also means He has no wife.
Ibn Kathir shows other ayahs that say how wrong it is to say Allah has a son. For example, everyone in the sky and the earth comes to Ar-Rahman only as a servant (Surah Maryam, 19:88–95).
The book Al-Jalalayn says He did not give birth, because no one is like Him. And He was not born, because being made is not for Him.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas says He does not have a son who will get His kingdom, and He did not get His kingdom from anyone.

prophet: The Prophet ﷺ taught his friend to say 'Say: He is Allah, One' and the two surahs of safety, Al-Falaq and An-Nas, three times in the evening and three times in the morning. He said: 'They will be enough for you.' (Abu Dawud, At-Tirmidhi and An-Nasa'i. At-Tirmidhi said hasan sahih gharib.)

Aisha said that every night when the Prophet ﷺ went to bed, he put his hands together and blew into them. Then he read Al-Ikhlas, Al-Falaq and An-Nas into them. Then he wiped his body with his hands, starting with his head and face. He did this three times. (Sahih al-Bukhari.)
scholars: Ibn Kathir explains: no one is like Him, no one is equal to Him, and nothing at all is even close to being like Him.
The book Tanwir al-Miqbas says He has no opposite and no partner who can compete with Him about His kingdom.
